title: Wingy Manone and rooming on Lawrence Avenue
summary: In an added tape Rinker recalls rooming with a depressed Wingy Manone, whose mother was ill, and the Loyacano brothers, and wonders if Art Hodes later lived there.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: John uh during the time I was talking before when I was here about the musicians I'd known that came from New Orleans. I forgot to mention several. Uh one of them was Wingy Minoni. I knew him of course through the years he was in Chicago during the 20s and 30s. Matter of fact I roomed with him for a while on Lawrence Avenue and uh that was a time when Wingy was quite depressed. He was uh worried about his mother who was I believe in New Orleans or someplace in Louisiana and she was ill at the time and he was quite worried about her. And there was Jack Locano, a trombone player. Do you remember where Wingy was working working in these days? He wasn't working much right then. Uh was it a hotel? No it was a rooming house. I moved away and Art may have moved in. I moved away and uh I was married at that time and I was married off and on.
